key_insight: Diagnostic accuracy can look good even when a medical LLM uses patient evidence in questionable ways, so the paper audits how evidence actually supports or conflicts with diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: This matters because clinicians and evaluators need to know whether a model’s answer is grounded in the case details or just reaching the right diagnosis by shortcut.
method: Decomposed each patient case into evidence units.
Scored candidate diagnoses under controlled evidence subsets.
Analyzed low-order evidence interactions and separated clinically plausible interactions from suspicious ones.
evidence_signal: Across DDXPlus, CupCase, and MedCase, faithful support plus differential conflict or cancellation explained most interaction strength, and a blinded 5-reviewer review of 130 enriched DDXPlus items found invalid or shortcut-like cases concentrated in negated/absent findings and local evidence.
watch_item: Because some large or negative evidence interactions are clinically reasonable differentials, the audit still needs robustness checks and clinical review before labeling a model failure.
paper_title: Auditing Evidence Use in Medical LLM Diagnosis
